I see that chat(init) with a sessionId just sets the session identifier without loading past messages—only loadChat() actually fetches the stored snapshot and populates the message history. So if agents.ts calls chat().send() without going through loadChat(), that's expected behavior by design: chat() starts fresh while loadChat() resumes a prior session.

Though the phrase "attaches to one via init" in the docs is a bit ambiguous, so I want to check the actual send() implementation to see whether the transport layer passes the sessionId in a way that lets the server continue the conversation server-side, even if the client hasn't loaded prior messages locally.

Looking at buildInit(), I see the priority order: snapshotId first, then clientState, then falling back to connectInit. So for session resumption with just a sessionId, none of those earlier fields are set, meaning connectInit itself—containing the sessionId—gets returned and passed along to the transport layer.

Now I need to trace what happens server-side when an init payload with only a sessionId (no snapshotId) arrives at a local in-process agent. I should search agent.mjs for where init.sessionId gets resolved to look up the stored session.

I'm noticing that resuming by sessionId requires the agent to have a store configured, but checking agents.ts shows orderAgent and triage lack a store while refundAgent has one—so there's a potential bug if a customer's session gets routed through an agent without store support.

I'm also wondering whether orderAgent needs its own store since delegation happens within triage's single session via historyLength, meaning the store likely only needs to live on triage itself. I should check how the "support chat" entry point is actually invoked—probably through the dev UI's agent chat interface, which would send a sessionId to whichever agent is wired up as the main entry point.

The root issue seems clear now: triage is defined without a store, so Dev UI's automatic session continuation fails with a "no store configured" error when it tries to resume by sessionId. The fix is adding a store to triage (and possibly orderAgent too, given the bug mentions a specific order flow), though a single first message would still work fine since no sessionId is needed until a follow-up turn.

I want to verify how resolveSession gets invoked and check whether the exact error path matches "chat cannot be picked up again by its session id," which would strongly support my hypothesis. Let me look at lines 320-420 in agent.mjs for the precise context.

Confirmed: without a `store`, any attempt to resume by `sessionId` throws `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. This matches the bug exactly — `triage` (the agent that fronts the support chat and delegates to `orderAgent`) has no `store`, so the second turn fails and the customer has to restart and repeat the order number. Let's check `orderAgent` too, since it's the one actually answering, and see how `agents()` delegation passes session/store context.

Confirmed: delegation passes recent conversation messages as client-managed state to orderAgent on each call, meaning orderAgent stays stateless with no sessionId or store—triage injects the relevant history each time, so orderAgent's context comes entirely from the parent session.

But triage's own session continuity across turns needs to persist via sessionId, which means triage itself must have a `store`. Without it, resuming by sessionId on the second turn throws FAILED_PRECONDITION, forcing a restart—exactly matching the reported bug where sessions can't be picked back up.

The fix is to add `store` to the triage agent definition, reusing the same store variable already used by refundAgent.

text: The fix works end-to-end: the second turn, resumed purely by `sessionId`, correctly recalls order A-1001 without the customer repeating it. Now clean up the test script and write `answer.json`.

## Summary

**Root cause:** In `src/agents.ts`, the `triage` agent — the entry point for the support chat, which delegates order questions to `orderAgent` — was defined without a session `store`. Genkit's agent runtime requires a `store` on any agent that's resumed via `sessionId`; without one it throws `FAILED_PRECONDITION: Cannot use 'sessionId' with agent 'triage': this agent has no store configured`. That's exactly why the follow-up turn ("What is its status?") couldn't be picked up by the session id, forcing the customer to restart and repeat the order number. A single question works fine because the first turn never needs to resume anything.

**Fix:** Added `store` (the same `FileSessionStore` already used by `refundAgent`) to the `triage` agent definition.

I verified it directly: reverting the one-line fix reproduces the exact `FAILED_PRECONDITION` error on a second call with the same `sessionId`; with the fix in place, a two-turn session ("My order is A-1001." → "What is its status?") correctly answers using the remembered order on the second turn, resumed purely by `sessionId`.

`answer.json` has been written in the project root with the file, broken snippet, cause, and evidence. No changes were made to `package.json` or dependencies.
